title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare and say your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use scare tactics to get you to act quickly.
example_message: "This is Medicare. We need to confirm your Social Security number or your coverage will be canceled immediately."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security or Medicare number
Pressures you to act right away
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn't be delivered and you need to click a link to reschedule or pay a fee. The link leads to a fake website that tries to steal your information or install malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your address and pay the $2.99 fee here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Asks you to click a link
what_to_do: Delete the text and do not click any links.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails that look like they're from the Social Security Administration. They claim there's a problem with your account and ask you to click a link or download an attachment.
example_message: "We noticed suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please click here to verify your information."
red_flags: Asks you to click a link or open an attachment
Poor grammar or odd sender address
what_to_do: Do not click links or download attachments. Go to the official Social Security website or call them if you’re concerned.

title: Facebook 'Friend in Need' Money Request
how_it_works: A scammer hacks a friend’s Facebook account and sends messages asking for money because of an emergency. They may say they are stranded or need help with a bill.
example_message: "Hi, I’m stuck out of town and need $500 to get home. Can you send it to me right away?"
red_flags: Unusual request for money from a friend
Asks for payment by gift card or wire transfer
what_to_do: Call your friend directly to check if the request is real before sending any money.

title: Tech Support Pop-Up Scam
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and must call a phone number for help. The scammer pretends to be from Microsoft or another big company and tries to get you to pay for fake repairs.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Tells you to call a phone number
Asks for payment or remote access to your computer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number. If you’re worried, contact a trusted local computer repair shop.
